drivers.name: ETC Eos Family Console
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls ETC Eos family lighting consoles (Apex, Ti, Gio, Ion Xe, Element 2, Nomad/Eos PC) via OSC. Fire cues, fire macros, recall snapshots and presets, fire palettes, set channel/group/submaster levels, send raw command-line strings, press hardkeys/softkeys. Status pushed by Eos: current/pending cue text, command line, Live/Blind state, active cue progress.

help.overview: Controls an ETC Eos family lighting console (Apex, Ti, Gio, Ion Xe, Element 2, Nomad, Eos PC) over OSC (Open Sound Control) via UDP. Fire cues, fire macros, recall snapshots and presets, fire palettes, set channel/group/submaster levels, send raw command-line strings, or press any hardkey/softkey. Eos pushes the current command line, active cue text, pending cue text, Live/Blind state, and active cue progress percentage automatically.
help.setup:
1. On the console: Setup > System > Show Control > OSC.
   Enable both OSC RX and OSC TX. Set OSC UDP RX to 8000 and OSC UDP
   TX to 8001 (or any pair you prefer, then mirror the values in
   this driver's config).
2. Set OSC TX IP to the OpenAVC server's IP address. Eos will send
   all /eos/out/... status to that address on the OSC TX port.
3. In OpenAVC: enter the console's IP address as Host. Leave Port
   at 8000 and Listen Port at 8001 unless you changed them on the
   console.
4. Hardkey names for the press_key command match the labels printed
   on the console face panel, in lowercase, with spaces replaced
   by underscores (e.g. "go", "stop", "go_to_cue", "live", "blind",
   "select_last", "clear_cmd_line"). The full list lives in the
   Eos Family Online Help under "OSC Key Names".

compatible_models.notes: All Eos-family consoles share the same OSC dictionary documented in the Eos Family Online Help. ColorSource AV exposes a subset of the same /eos OSC namespace.

drivers.name: ETC Paradigm
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls ETC Paradigm architectural lighting processors (P-ACP-E Mk2, P-ACP-D Mk2) through the Paradigm Serial Access Protocol over UDP or RS-232. List the channels, groups, presets, sequences, spaces, walls, macros and overrides to control by their LightDesigner names; each one shows its level or state.

help.overview: Controls an ETC Paradigm processor through PSAP, the Paradigm Serial Access Protocol. Each channel, group, preset, sequence, space, wall, macro and override you list under Objects appears under the device: a channel's or group's level, a preset's state (active, inactive or altered), a sequence's, a macro's, a wall's (open or closed) and an override's. Commands set levels, activate presets, start sequences, turn spaces off, open walls, run macros and enable overrides. Send PSAP Command sends any line, including a UString set up in LightDesigner.
help.setup:
1. In LightDesigner, select the processor and expand UDP Serial Config. Set Input UDP Port to a port from 4703 to 4727 (4703 here by default) and Input Handler to PSAP 6.0.0, then upload the configuration. For RS-232 instead, RS232 Serial Config already uses PSAP 6.0.0 at 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.
2. Leave End of Message Char at CR unless the site uses another, and set the same here.
3. In OpenAVC, enter the processor's IP address and the UDP port, or pick Direct serial and the serial port.
4. Under Objects, add a row for each thing to control: its type, its name exactly as LightDesigner shows it (case included), and the space that holds it. Fill in the space: a fade time needs it, and the processor reads a name in that space only. PSAP cannot read a name with a comma or a colon in it.
5. Optional: add PSAP Triggers in LightDesigner (user access Advanced) for the objects listed, so their changes show at once instead of at the next poll. Over RS-232 they arrive on the serial line. Over UDP, ETC's PSAP guide does not say where a trigger is sent: if LightDesigner lets you send it to an IP address and UDP port, use this computer's address and a free port, and enter that port as Trigger Port here (OpenAVC 0.40.0 or later). The poll still reads every listed object either way.

compatible_models.notes: Paradigm Processor Mk2 (Enclosure and DIN), on Paradigm 6.0.0 or later with the PSAP 6.0.0 Input Handler. Status updates arrive on their own over RS-232 when the LightDesigner configuration has PSAP Triggers; over UDP they are read by polling.

drivers.name: Art-Net DMX (Generic)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Sends DMX512 lighting data over Art-Net (UDP 6454) to any Art-Net-compatible node, gateway, fixture, or controller. Maintains a 512-byte channel buffer per universe in memory; commands set channels, blackout, or full-on; a periodic keep-alive re-broadcast keeps long-running shows alive on receivers that time out idle universes.

help.overview: Art-Net is the de-facto Ethernet protocol for DMX512 lighting. Controllers send ArtDmx packets to nodes (Art-Net to DMX gateways), or directly to network-native fixtures. The driver maintains a 512-channel buffer for each universe it controls and re-broadcasts on a 900 ms keep-alive cadence so the receiver doesn't drop the universe.
help.setup:
1. Set the target node's IP to a static address and put it on the same VLAN as the OpenAVC server. Art-Net traditionally uses the 2.x.x.x or 10.x.x.x range, but any reachable IP works.
2. Confirm the node's universe number — Art-Net calls it the Port-Address (0..32767). Most consoles and fixtures expose it as a Net + Subnet + Universe trio (7 + 4 + 4 bits); enter the combined 15-bit value here. Universe 0 is a common default.
3. To broadcast (one transmit reaches all nodes on the subnet), use the broadcast IP for your subnet. Unicast to a node's IP is preferred per the Art-Net 4 spec.
4. Run the ``set_channel`` or ``blackout`` command. The driver starts re-broadcasting automatically; no separate ``start`` is needed.

models: Art-Net Node / Gateway / Fixture (any conforming vendor)
compatible_models.notes: Art-Net is an open published standard maintained by Artistic Licence. This driver sends ArtDmx and works with any conforming Art-Net receiver. Brand-specific entries below name the major node / gateway / fixture vendors confirmed by their published product literature.

ETC's Response and Net3 gateway families translate Art-Net (and sACN) to physical DMX outputs. ETC's Eos console is also covered by the dedicated `etc_eos` OSC driver, which is the right choice when controlling cues directly rather than driving fixtures.
Pathway Pathport gateways translate Art-Net and sACN to DMX. Common in pro AV and theatrical installs.
Enttec ODE family converts Art-Net to DMX. ODE Mk3 also speaks sACN. The smaller-footprint DIN-ODE fits a DIN rail in install racks.
Elation E-Node series Art-Net / sACN to DMX gateways.
Chauvet Professional network nodes for entertainment lighting.
American DJ network DMX gateways.
Color Kinetics (Signify) architectural LED gateways. The controller side speaks Art-Net to drive Color Kinetics fixtures via PDS power/data supplies and Antumbra controllers.

MA Lighting Network Processing Units translate console output to Art-Net and sACN for downstream gateways. Useful for tracking backup or for sending Art-Net into an MA console for visualizer / pre-program workflows.
Madrix is primarily an Art-Net source for LED video pixel-mapping, but its Aura and Plexus hardware bridges accept Art-Net input and convert to DMX or playback stored shows.

drivers.name: sACN / E1.31 DMX (Generic)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Streams DMX512 lighting data over sACN (Streaming ACN, ANSI E1.31) to any sACN-compatible node, gateway, fixture, or controller. Uses per-universe multicast (239.255.x.x, UDP 5568) by default, or unicast to a specific node. Maintains a 512-byte channel buffer per universe in memory; commands set channels, blackout, or full-on; per-source priority tunes multi-source merging; a keep-alive re-send holds static looks alive and a graceful stream-termination releases the universe on disconnect.

help.overview: sACN (Streaming ACN, ANSI E1.31) is the open ANSI standard for DMX512 over IP. Controllers send E1.31 Data Packets to nodes (sACN-to-DMX gateways) or directly to network-native fixtures. Each universe has its own multicast group (239.255.<hi>.<lo>), so traffic reaches only the receivers that joined it. The driver keeps a 512-channel buffer per universe, re-sends on a ~900 ms keep-alive cadence so a static look never times out, and stamps a per-source priority for multi-source merging.
help.setup:
1. Put the sACN node/gateway on the same VLAN as the OpenAVC server and confirm its universe number (1..63999).
2. Leave Addressing on 'Multicast' (the sACN default) unless the node is configured for unicast — multicast is derived automatically as 239.255.<hi>.<lo> from the universe, so nothing else to enter. For 'Unicast', fill in the node's IP as the Target Host.
3. Set the Priority if the universe has more than one source (higher wins; default 100). Set a Source Name so the universe is identifiable on the network.
4. Run set_channel / blackout / full_on. The driver starts sending and re-broadcasting automatically; no separate start is needed. On disconnect it sends a graceful stream-termination so receivers release the universe immediately.

models: sACN / E1.31 Node / Gateway / Fixture (any conforming vendor)
compatible_models.notes: sACN is the ANSI E1.31 public standard maintained by ESTA. This driver sends E1.31 Data Packets and works with any conforming sACN receiver. Brand entries below name major node / gateway / fixture vendors confirmed by their published product literature.

ETC's Response and Net3 gateway families translate sACN (and Art-Net) to physical DMX outputs. ETC's Eos console is also covered by the dedicated etc_eos OSC driver, which is the right choice when controlling cues directly rather than driving fixtures.
Pathway Pathport gateways translate sACN and Art-Net to DMX. Common in pro AV and theatrical installs; sACN is Pathway's preferred network protocol.
Enttec ODE Mk3 and S-Play families accept sACN and convert to DMX. The DIN-ODE fits a DIN rail in install racks.
Elation E-Node series sACN / Art-Net to DMX gateways.
Chauvet Professional network nodes for entertainment lighting; sACN and Art-Net capable.
Color Kinetics (Signify) architectural LED gateways. The controller side speaks sACN to drive Color Kinetics fixtures via PDS power/data supplies and Antumbra controllers.
MA Lighting Network Processing Units translate console output to sACN and Art-Net for downstream gateways.
Madrix is primarily an sACN / Art-Net source for LED pixel-mapping, but its Aura and Plexus hardware bridges accept sACN input and convert to DMX or play back shows.

drivers.name: Lutron HomeWorks QS
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Lutron HomeWorks QS Processors (HQP6-2, HQP7) over Telnet using the Lutron Integration Protocol (LIP). Supports zone level control (OUTPUT), keypad/phantom button presses and LED control (DEVICE), area occupancy queries (AREA), and shade group control (SHADEGRP). Use phantom keypad button presses to activate scenes.

help.overview: Lutron HomeWorks QS is a residential and small-commercial lighting, shade, and HVAC control system. The HomeWorks QS Processor exposes a Telnet integration protocol (LIP) on port 23 that lets external controllers raise/lower lights and shades, press phantom keypad buttons (which activate scenes programmed in the Lutron design software), and monitor occupancy.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the HomeWorks QS Processor's IP address (set a static
   reservation on the network).
2. In the HomeWorks QS Design software, on the Integration tab,
   assign Integration IDs to the outputs, devices (keypads), areas,
   and shade groups you want to control. Note them down — you'll
   reference them in macros and triggers.
3. Confirm a Telnet login exists for integration use. Defaults are
   "lutron" / "integration" but the integrator may have changed
   them in the design software. Enter the username and password
   in the device config below.
4. To activate a scene: program a phantom keypad in the design
   software, assign each button to a scene, then use the
   "Press Button" command with that keypad's Integration ID and
   the button's Component Number.
5. Zone (OUTPUT) levels are 0-100 percent. Fade and Delay times
   are optional and accept SS.ss, SS, MM:SS, or HH:MM:SS formats.

compatible_models.notes: HomeWorks QS Processor (HQP6-2 and HQP7). Other Lutron systems (RadioRA 3, Caseta SB Pro, Athena, QS Standalone) speak related but distinct protocol surfaces and are not covered by this driver.

drivers.name: Pharos Designer LPC
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Control Pharos Designer 2 lighting projects on LPC and LPC X controllers. Start named scenes and timelines, dim fixture groups, run project triggers, and follow live playback and controller status.

help.overview: Use the scenes, timelines, fixture groups and triggers programmed in Designer. Commands propagate across the Pharos project. Playback state and Affecting Output are separate: a running timeline may be hidden by higher-priority playback. Group master intensity multiplies programmed output; it does not replace the lighting look.
help.setup:
1. Upload a Designer 2 project to the LPC or LPC X. Select API version 8 or later in its project properties (version 12 recommended).
2. Enter the controller management address and web port. For HTTPS, enable Use HTTPS and enter the HTTPS port. Enable Verify Certificate only with a certificate trusted by this computer.
3. If controller security is enabled, enter an account permitted to read status and control playback. Leave both credentials blank only when security is disabled.
4. Named controls load automatically. Use Refresh from Device after editing the project; the periodic refresh also detects changes. Keep Poll Interval above zero to refresh project names and membership.
5. Use Start Scene or Start Timeline to layer playback. Start in Playback Group replaces only that group’s playback. Use Release to fade it out.
6. Designer owns fixture programming, networking and user accounts. Open Web UI opens the controller’s own pages.

compatible_models.notes: Designer 2 with project API version 8 or later. Built from Designer API v12 documentation; not tested on hardware. Express and ETC Mosaic are not included.

drivers.name: Philips Hue Bridge
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Philips Hue lights, rooms, zones, and scenes via the CLIP v2 API on a Hue Bridge (HTTPS). Live push state from the bridge's event stream; every light and group is a child entity; pair with the bridge's link button straight from the device page. Requires the square v2 bridge (BSB002).

help.overview:
Philips Hue is the most widely deployed residential and small-commercial smart-lighting platform. The bridge sits on the LAN and bridges Zigbee bulbs / fixtures to a local REST API. AV integrators commonly use it for accent lighting in boardrooms, hospitality spaces, and houses of worship — recall a "Presentation" scene when the projector turns on, fade up "Q&A" lighting when the session ends.

Every light and every group (room / zone, plus the whole-home "All Lights" group) appears as a child entity with live on/brightness/color state pushed by the bridge the moment it changes — including changes made from the Hue app or Hue dimmer switches. Scenes are offered in a picker on the recall command.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP (or DHCP reservation) on the Hue Bridge in your router. The bridge is also discoverable via mDNS.
2. Add the device with the bridge's IP address, leaving the App Key blank.
3. Press the round link button on top of the bridge, then run the "Pair with Bridge (Link Button)" action from this device's page within 30 seconds. It requests an app key, saves it, and reconnects automatically.
4. Lights, groups, and scenes are enumerated on connect and stay in sync live — new fixtures added in the Hue app appear on their own.
5. Commands that act on a light or group offer a picker of the discovered children; the recall command offers a scene picker. Brightness and color commands take an optional transition time for smooth fades.

compatible_models.notes: Verified against a BSB002 bridge (firmware 1.78.1978074000): HTTPS + application-key connect, enumeration of a 19-light install with rooms/zones/scenes, live event-stream updates, and a light write confirmed back over the stream. The CLIP v2 API requires firmware 1948086000 or newer (any bridge updated since late 2019). The link-button pairing flow is unchanged from the previous driver generation, which was verified on the same bridge.

drivers.name: Visual Productions CueCore3
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Run installed lighting cues across sixteen playbacks. Follow playback activity, cue number, intensity and speed changes, with master controls and a reachability check.

help.overview: Use Next Cue, Previous Cue or Jump to Cue on a programmed playback. CueCore3 sends change notifications to its four most recent OSC clients. Values show the last report from the controller. After a network outage the current cue or intensity can remain unknown or show the previous report until that property changes. Hello checks connectivity only.
help.setup: Use the default API prefix core, and match the OSC Input Port on the Settings page (Figure 5.6 shows 8000). Disable OSC Forward so incoming control messages do not echo as feedback. Enter the unicast device address. Each playback number corresponds to the same number on the Playback page.
help.connection: OpenAVC registers by sending /core/hello and repeats it periodically. Reserve one of the four OSC client slots for OpenAVC. Use Identify to blink the controller LED when commissioning.

compatible_models.notes: CueCore3 Manual, firmware 1.30.25, Appendix E.
